<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
Allow terminals used by the **Copilot** harness on Windows to be opened in the Terminal view, so I can scroll through the full buffer and interact with them, the same way the **Local** harness allows.

## Current behavior

- **Local harness:** commands the agent runs execute in real terminals. I can bring any of them forward in the Terminal view to scroll the buffer, inspect output, or type into a running process.
- **Copilot harness on Windows:** commands run through the Copilot SDK's built-in shell tool. Their output is only shown inline in the chat as a read-only output stream. There is no terminal behind it, so nothing appears in the Terminal view and I cannot scroll the full buffer or interact with the process.

`chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled` would route Copilot sessions through Agent Host's own terminal tool, which creates real terminals that can be shown in the Terminal view. However, it is forced off on Windows (`process.platform !== 'win32'` in both `copilotSessionLauncher.ts` and `copilotSessionSandbox.ts`), and its description says "Not supported on Windows, where sessions use the SDK's terminal and sandbox runtime." Setting it to `true` on Windows has no effect.

## Requested behavior

On Windows, Copilot harness sessions should be able to use terminals that can be revealed in the Terminal view, for example by:

1. supporting `chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled` on Windows, or
2. opening the SDK shell tool's output in the Terminal view (read-only is still useful), with interaction where the runtime allows it.

## Motivation

- **Parity with the Local harness.** Switching harnesses currently drops a workflow I rely on.
- **Inspecting long output.** The inline chat output is not a good place to scroll through long build, test, or log output. A real terminal buffer with search and scrollback is.
- **Interacting with processes.** When a command prompts for input, hangs, or a long-running server needs attention, I need to type into it or stop it myself instead of asking the agent.
- **Debugging agent behavior.** Seeing exactly what ran, in the same shell and environment, makes it much easier to understand why a command failed.
items.title: Copilot Harness on Windows: Allow agent terminals to be opened in the Terminal view

items.body:
`setProperty(text, [lastIndex], undefined)` in `src/vs/base/common/jsonEdit.ts:118` removes one character too few:

```ts
edit = { offset, length: parentEndOffset - 2 - offset, content: '' };   // should be - 1
```

`parentEndOffset - 1` is the `]`, so `- 2` leaves the character before it. When that character belongs to the removed element:

- `[1, 2]` → remove index 1 → `[12]` (the value silently changes)
- `["x","y"]` → `["x""]` (invalid JSON)
- a CRLF keybindings.json (the Windows default) gets a bare `\n` before `]`

Where users hit it: **Remove Keybinding** / **Reset Keybinding** in the Keyboard Shortcuts editor (`keybindingEditing.ts:148,171`; new keybindings are appended, so removing the one just added is the last item), and deleting a chat hook (`aiCustomizationManagement.contribution.ts:393`), which writes straight to disk. Formatted LF files are not affected because a newline sits before `]`.

The same line was fixed upstream in microsoft/node-jsonc-parser (#108 / PR #120, merged 2026-05); VS Code's copy in `base/common` was not updated.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Write `keybindings.json` as `[{"key":"ctrl+a","command":"a"},{"key":"ctrl+b","command":"b"}]` (compact, as tools write it).
2. In the Keyboard Shortcuts editor, remove the `ctrl+b` keybinding.
3. The file no longer parses.

I have the one-character fix with tests and will open a PR referencing this issue.

- VS Code version: main b1dcc2d8 (2026-10-14)
- OS version: all (logic is platform-independent)

Disclosure: this was found, reproduced and patched by an AI agent (Claude Code), which ran the reproduction and tests quoted above. It has not been separately reviewed by a human.

<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not applicable. This issue concerns Agent Host.
- VS Code Version: Source code before PR #341671. The affected release version is not confirmed.
- OS Version: Not confirmed with a live reproduction.
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent Host session permissions in editor chat and the Agents window.
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Not specified.
- Logs: No live reproduction logs are attached.

## Problem

The session sandbox toggle is locked when managed policy enables sandboxing. It stays locked when the same policy permits bypass. The user cannot turn sandboxing off for the session from the permissions menu.

This is a follow-up to the closed issue #334265. PR #341671 addresses the current Agent Host behavior.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use a build without PR #341671 and a host that supports sandboxing.

1. Configure the effective managed policy with these values:

   ```json
   {
     "sandbox": {
       "enabled": true,
       "allowBypass": true
     }
   }
   ```

2. Start a Copilot CLI session through Agent Host.
3. Wait for the host to apply the managed policy. Make sure sandboxing is On.
4. Open the session permissions menu in editor chat.
5. Try to turn **Sandboxing for terminal** Off.
6. Repeat the check in the Agents window.

## Actual Result

The toggle is On and disabled. The user cannot request Off, although the policy permits bypass.

## Expected Result

- Keep the toggle editable when managed policy permits bypass.
- Apply an explicit user request to this session only. Do not change the global setting.
- Use the runtime session command. Do not treat a configuration update as approval to bypass managed policy.
- Change the applied state only after the runtime confirms the request.
- Keep the toggle On and disabled when managed policy forbids bypass.

## Check a Rejected Request

After the toggle is editable, check this failure case:

1. Start with sandboxing On.
2. Start an agent turn and keep it active.
3. Open the permissions menu and select Off.
4. Keep the menu open until the runtime rejects the change because the agent is active.
5. Close the menu. Then open it again.

Expected results:

- Show the runtime error.
- Restore the session configuration to the last applied value: On.
- Keep the rejected Off selection visible while the same menu stays open.
- Show On in the collapsed control.
- Show On when the user opens the menu again.
- Do not repeat the rejected disable command during configuration rollback.

## Verification Status

The locked-toggle behavior was confirmed by source inspection. The steps above have not been run in a live window for this report. The rejected-request steps describe a regression check for the fix, not a reproduction of the locked toggle.
items.title: Agent Host sandbox toggle is locked when managed policy permits bypass
